nodes.summary: For every bit $c$ and all natural numbers $m$ and $n$, the ripple-carry sum, with carry-in $c$, of the canonical binary expansions of $m$ and $n$ (least significant bit first, no trailing false bit) is the canonical binary expansion of $m + n + c$, where $c$ counts as $1$ if true and $0$ if false. In particular the sum stays canonical.
nodes.title: Addition is correct on canonical numbers

nodes.summary: For a carry-in bit $c$ and bit lists $u$ and $p$, both least significant bit first, the ripple-carry sum walks $p$. If $p$ is empty, the result is $u$ with the carry $c$ added (a final carry becomes a new last bit). Otherwise, with $a$ the first bit of $u$ ($a$ is false when $u$ is empty) and $b$ the first bit of $p$, the result is the bit $a \oplus b \oplus c$ followed by the ripple-carry sum of the rest of $u$…
nodes.title: Ripple-carry addition of bit lists

nodes.summary: For bits $a$, $b$ and a carry-in $c$, the carry out of adding $a$, $b$ and $c$ is $(a \wedge b) \vee (c \wedge (a \oplus b))$, which is true iff at least two of $a$, $b$, $c$ are true.
nodes.title: Carry bit of a full adder

nodes.summary: For every bit string $x$, every list $a$ of natural numbers and every natural number $t$, the SUBSET-SUM decoder returns the instance $(a, t)$ on $x$ if and only if $x$ is the encoding of the SUBSET-SUM instance with numbers $a$ and target $t$.
nodes.title: Decoding a SUBSET-SUM instance inverts its encoding

nodes.summary: A block holding a bit string $p$ writes each bit $b$ of $p$ as the two bits $1, b$ and ends with a single $0$. The decoder reads a bit string $x$ as one block holding the target $t$, followed by blocks holding numbers $a_1, \dots, a_n$ that run exactly to the end of $x$, where each block must hold the canonical binary representation of its number (least significant bit first, no trailing $0$). It returns the list…
nodes.title: Decoding a SUBSET-SUM instance

nodes.summary: For every bit string $p$, encoding in binary (least significant bit first) the natural number that $p$ decodes to gives back $p$ if and only if the trailing-zero test, started with no trailing zero, reports that $p$ does not end in $0$; that is, $p$ is empty or its last bit is $1$.
nodes.title: Canonical binary strings are those not ending in zero

nodes.summary: If $l$ is a sublist of a list $a$ of natural numbers, then there is a list $w$ of Booleans of the same length as $a$ such that the entries $a_i$ of $a$ with $w_i$ true, taken in order, form exactly $l$.
nodes.title: Every sublist is selected by a mask

nodes.summary: Let $k$ be a natural number, $v$ a value of the machine's Boolean flag and $S$ an assignment of contents to the stacks, and list the binary digits of $k$ least significant first, without leading zeros (so there are none for $k = 0$). Suppose stack $A$ holds $k$ copies of the unit symbol and stack $H$ is empty. Then, starting at label $\mathrm{hv}$ with flag $v$ and stacks $S$, the machine reaches label…
nodes.title: Binary conversion (SUBSET-SUM reduction machine)

nodes.summary: For a carry bit $c$ and a bit string $u$ (least significant bit first), $\mathrm{inc}(c, u)$ adds $c$ to $u$ by ripple carry: on the empty string it is $[1]$ if $c$ is true and empty otherwise, and on a string with first bit $a$ and rest $u'$ it is the bit $a \oplus c$ followed by $\mathrm{inc}(a \wedge c, u')$.
nodes.title: Adding a carry bit

nodes.summary: The verifier has seven stacks: the input $X$, the witness $W$, the target $T$ (most significant bit on top), the running sum $A$ (least significant bit on top), the new sum $B$ (most significant bit on top), and the scratch stacks $P$ and $Q$ of the final comparison.
nodes.title: Stacks of the SUBSET-SUM verifier

nodes.summary: The verifier has the labels $\mathrm{tgt}(z)$, reading the target; $\mathrm{next}$, starting the next number; $\mathrm{add}(c, z)$, adding a chosen number with carry $c$; $\mathrm{skip}(z)$, skipping an unchosen number; $\mathrm{fin}(c)$, carrying $c$ through the rest of the sum; $\mathrm{back}$, moving the new sum back; $\mathrm{fmove}$, moving the final sum for the comparison; $\mathrm{cmp}$, comparing;…
nodes.title: Labels of the SUBSET-SUM verifier

nodes.summary: For a Boolean $z$ and a list of bits $p$, the value is $z$ when $p$ is empty and the negation of the last bit of $p$ otherwise. So if $z$ records whether the bits read so far end in false, the value records whether those bits followed by $p$ end in false.
nodes.title: Whether a bit string ends in false

nodes.summary: For a fuel $n$ and a list of bits $r$, the result is either a list of numbers or a failure. If $r$ is empty, the result is the empty list. If $r$ is non-empty and $n = 0$, parsing fails. If $r$ is non-empty and $n = m + 1$, one prefix-coded number is decoded off the front of $r$: if this gives a number $a$ with remainder $r'$, the result is $a$ followed by the result for $r'$ with fuel $m$ (failing if that fails),…
nodes.title: Parsing number blocks, with fuel

nodes.summary: For a list of numbers $a_0, \dots, a_{k-1}$ and a list of bits $w$, the list of those $a_i$ with $w_i$ true, in their original order, where positions $i$ beyond the end of $w$ count as false.
nodes.title: Numbers chosen by a mask

nodes.summary: Let $x$ be a bit string. Start the VERTEX-COVER to SUBSET-SUM machine at its start label with any state bit and with stacks in which the input stack $\mathsf{X}$ holds the bit symbols of $x$, first bit on top, and every other stack is empty. Then within at most $40(|x| + 1)^4$ steps the machine reaches the label $\mathsf{done}$ with some state bit and stacks in which the output stack $\mathsf{O}$ holds, top first,…
nodes.title: Run of the VERTEX-COVER to SUBSET-SUM machine

nodes.summary: For bit strings $x$ and $w$, the verifier accepts $(x, w)$ exactly when $x$ is the encoding of a SUBSET-SUM instance with numbers $a_0, \dots, a_{n-1}$ and target $t$, and the sum of the $a_i$ for which bit $i$ of $w$ is true equals $t$; bits beyond the end of $w$ count as false, and bits of $w$ past position $n - 1$ are ignored. If $x$ is not the encoding of an instance, the verifier rejects.
nodes.title: The SUBSET-SUM verifier

nodes.summary: The statements of the SUBSET-SUM verifier machine are the statements of a multi-stack Turing machine in Mathlib's TM2 model whose stacks are the seven stacks $X$, $W$, $T$, $A$, $B$, $P$, $Q$, each over the symbol alphabet of the SAT verifier, whose labels are the labels of the SUBSET-SUM verifier, and whose local state is a Boolean.
nodes.title: Statements of the SUBSET-SUM verifier

nodes.summary: A bit string $x$ is a yes-instance of SUBSET-SUM if and only if there is a bit string $w$ with $|w| \le |x|$ such that the SUBSET-SUM verifier accepts $(x, w)$.
nodes.title: SUBSET-SUM is characterized by its verifier

nodes.summary: Let $l = (b_1, \dots, b_m)$ be a list of bits. Start the VERTEX-COVER to SUBSET-SUM machine at label $\mathsf{tem}$ with any state bit and with stacks $S$ in which stack $\mathsf{T}$ holds exactly the bit symbols of $b_1, \dots, b_m$, top first. Then after exactly $m + 1$ steps the machine is at label $\mathsf{done}$ with some state bit and stacks $S'$ in which the output stack $\mathsf{O}$ holds, top first,…
nodes.title: Run of the target-bit loop of the subset-sum emitter

nodes.summary: Let $l$ be a list of bits, let $l'$ be $l$ with its leading $\mathrm{false}$ bits removed, and let $o$ be a list of bits. Start the VERTEX-COVER to SUBSET-SUM machine at label $\mathsf{tsk}$ with any state bit and with stacks $S$ in which stack $\mathsf{T}$ holds exactly the bit symbols of $l$, first bit on top, and the output stack $\mathsf{O}$ holds $\mathrm{false}$ followed by $o$. Then after exactly $|l| + 1$…
nodes.title: Run of the target-output phase of the subset-sum emitter

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
